search_window.basis: The start is completed_at from the immediately preceding verified Food Line Source Watch ledger heartbeat on 2026-10-27. The end is Pacific observation time after the bounded searches. Publication and crawl recency do not establish incident novelty.

search_terms: "food bank" fire flood closure October 26 2026 distribution
focus_classes: Only/sole/last/full-service grocery store loss, closure, fire, or disaster
Emergency distribution cancellation or suspension due to storm, flood, fire, outage, or facility damage
Abrupt pantry/food bank closure or major access reduction
Official SNAP/WIC/food assistance interruption with immediate access consequences

coverage_notes: Supplementary recall only. Nationwide production collection remains authoritative and was not accessed or modified.
Twelve targeted web searches were completed across all four specified high-value miss classes; search tool did not report failures.
No date-verified, newly reported qualifying U.S. food-access disruption was found within the Pacific observation window. This is not proof that none occurred.
Only-grocery-store fire results for Spencer, New York were dated September 14–15, 2026, predating the recall window. Earlier Wilson, New York and other grocery results also fell outside the window.

Searches for canceled distributions or pantry/food-bank closures primarily returned historical incidents: Ruby's Pantry's April 2026 closure; a Portsmouth, Virginia pantry closure months earlier; and older storms. The May 2026 Baker Lake food-bank fire was in Canada and outside geographic scope.
Official SNAP/WIC interruption searches prominently surfaced 2025 federal shutdown reporting, not a new official interruption within the target window.
Searches excluded old stories, non-U.S. events, routine scheduled closures, donation appeals, generic program news, and unrelated disaster or water-distribution stories.
Local provider notices, unindexed social media announcements, and events reported after the observation time can be missed by web indexing.
No editorial approvals, publication, public content changes, schedule modifications or task disabling.
